projects.title: Show HN: Open Source AI Employees
projects.author: DotSauce
projects.summary: Fable 5 scored 99.19% on WebVoyager a few months ago, a be A benchmark is not your logged-in admin panel. Browser use agents are no longer demos. I believe this is a big tipping point. I have been a web developer for most of my career and building with AI agents for nearly four years. Last October I wrote that the missing piece was browser agents reliable enough to leave alone. So I published this open source repo, so everyone can have high quality AI employees. They are, for the most part, agent harness agnostic and can work on any of them. An AI Employee is a folder of plain text routines that covers one business role: SEO, social, sales, support, web dev, ads, launch work, and a chief of staff that reads the other employees' logs. Eight roles, 60 routines, MIT. They run on your own machine through the agent harness you already use, and they drive your own signed-in browser. Two of the big things that make my agents better: - Recursive self improvement reinforcement - Custom trained recipes to get meaningful work done in browser There's also some other neat features and more planned. Like only-when-needed push notifications for Claude Code and other harnesses that support that. I'm also building in community recipe and ecosystem contribution. Agents may discover workflows or tricks for high level tasks and contribute them to all other agent operators. They run a lot of my own business every day now. One example: full meta ad campaigns, content marketing, SEO, backlink building, community management, app development and management. I recommend you start with one that can take on the work you don't want to do. Or replace yourself. Happy to answer any questions.

projects.title: Pace — Pi coding agent 的桌面 GUI（开源 / early）
projects.author: kieranx
projects.summary: 大家好！介绍一下 Pace ，给 Pi coding agent 用的桌面 GUI 。 TL;DR Pace 是一个为 Pi Coding Agent 打造的开源桌面 GUI Workbench （基于 Electron + React ）。它不是简单的 API 套壳，而是把 Pi 作为后端独立引擎驱动的工作台，提供可视化的执行轨迹、Diff 审查、Token 成本透视以及子代理观察能力。 GitHub： https://github.com/BubblePtr/pace ![home page]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bubbleptr/pace/main/docs/assets/readme/home.png) **1 、为什么做 Pace?** 平时高强度使用终端里的 Coding Agent （如 Pi ）时，常常遇到几个痛点： - 滚屏混乱与失焦：任务一长、Tool Call 一多，几十屏的日志很难快速回溯「它刚才具体改了什么、哪一步报错了」。 - Diff 审查与终端挤占：代码改动需要反复切另外的 git 工具去看，或者在命令行里看折叠 diff ，不够直观。 - Token 与成本黑盒：很多工具只给一个最后的花销，中间过程每一步吃了多少 context 、cache 命中情况到底怎样，缺少真凭实据。 - 子代理（ Subagent ）观测困难：多 agent 协作或并发长任务时，终端里交错的日志基本没法看。 - 既然 Pi 的架构本身把底层 Engine 和扩展能力做得非常干净，那最顺手的形态应该是一个像 IDE 一样的桌面 Workbench ，而不是只留在终端里。 **2 、 它和常见的套壳工具有什么区别** - 直接集成 Pi 官方 SDK：Pace 不是在外部起一个 CLI 命令做文本解析，而是直接集成 Pi 官方 SDK （基于 SDK Driver / createAgentSession 驱动 Agent 运行时）。Pi 本地的 Session 日志是唯一数据源，终端里跑过的会话可以直接在 Pace 中打开，所有原生的配置、插件和会话数据完全同构复用。 - 把舞台留给插件：专设插件面板（ Extension Surfaces ）：我们不想把所有功能做死在主界面，而是为插件提供可视化的舞台。在 Session Dock 中规划了专属的插件面板接口。未来各类插件不再局限于在终端里打日志，而是可以按插件自身需求，注册并渲染独特的交互窗口（例如子代理树状拓扑、自定义工作流检查器、测试结果仪表盘等）。 - Session Dock 边聊边看：侧边集成 Changes (Diff 审查)、Files 、Terminal 、Browser 等面板，审代码、看终端输出不需要反复切屏。 - Trajectory 轨迹与成本真相：完整的执行轨迹流，细化到每一步 Tool Call 的耗时、入参/返回，以及真实的 Token 与费用账单。 - 子代理链路观察：支持关联到子会话回放（ Subagent ），不再是一团黑盒。 **3 、技术实现与架构** - 桌面壳：Electron （主进程 + utilityProcess 独立运行后端 + React 渲染层）。 - 前端架构：React 19 + TypeScript + Astryx 设计系统规范。 - 通信与状态：进程隔离，通过规范化的事件流做状态投影，保证长任务或断网崩溃时主界面不卡顿、数据不丢。 **4 、目前状态与交流** 目前项目处于早期快速迭代阶段，基础的工作流和 Trajectory / Diff / 子代理观测链路已经可用。 想和大家交流： 大家平时更习惯纯 CLI 的 Agent 交互，还是希望有一个专门的 GUI 工作台来辅助审查和调度？ 在多 Agent 或复杂工作流场景下，你最希望在 GUI 上看到哪些维度的信息？ 欢迎试用体验、提 Issue 或拍砖！

projects.title: vibe 了个功能丰富的微博网页版美化和屏蔽插件，老哥们需要的自取
projects.author: gay4in
projects.summary: 折腾了一个微博网页版插件，叫「全能围脖」，有 Chrome 扩展版和油猴脚本版。 ![05-顶部宣传图.png]( ) ![01-统一设置.png]( ) ![02-日间配色.png]( ) ![03-夜间配色.png]( ) 起因也很简单：平时还会用电脑刷微博，但页面上不想看的东西有点多，美化、屏蔽和下载又经常要装好几个脚本。昨天看到 @aslan1 大佬的分享，索性借助 codex 折腾了一下，把这些功能整合到一个设置面板里，按需开关。上架了 chrome 插件商店 主要能做这些： - **页面美化**：调整卡片排版、图文比例，有 5 组日夜配色，也可以自定义文字和背景颜色；侧栏、发布框、Logo 等可以按喜好隐藏。 - **快速内容屏蔽**：支持关键词、正则、来源、超话等过滤，以及广告清理、AI 内容和过期微博过滤。以及即时点击用户屏蔽。 - **用户名单管理**：按 UID 过滤用户，支持名单导入导出、官方黑名单同步，在帖子、评论、搜索等场景里过滤不想看的内容。 - **时间线和页面精简**：可以切换最新时间线，调整推荐内容、导航和侧栏的显示。 - **截图和媒体工具**：Markdown 导出，图片、视频、LivePhoto 的选择与打包下载 功能看起来比较多，不过分成了四个模块，不需要的直接关掉就行。装好后刷新微博，点击右下角「围脖」就能打开设置。 先说明一下来源：这是基于 **MWCA 、微博综合屏蔽、Pynseq 、微博浏览助手** 做的整合和改造，保留了上游作者及许可说明，感谢原作者们的工作。 **安装地址：** - [Chrome 扩展版]( https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/pgginmnckecopnboblpbipalejimpnoj?utm_source=item-share-cb) - [油猴脚本版（ Greasy Fork ）]( https://greasyfork.org/zh-CN/scripts/596500) 扩展版和脚本版选一个装就行；如果已经装了上面提到的同类脚本，建议先停用，避免功能重复或冲突。 主要面向桌面网页版微博，微博改版后部分功能可能需要继续适配。老哥们有需要的可以试试，遇到 bug 或者有什么想要的功能，欢迎回帖。报问题时带一下浏览器版本、出问题的页面和复现步骤，方便我排查。

projects.title: [开源]「Flotilla v1.0.0：让 AI 一次管理所有服务器，但每一步都过人审批」
projects.author: MuskZhou
projects.summary: > 本人文笔不佳，写不出想表达的意思，以下内容有部分是 ai 代笔后我再进行更改，或者让 ai 帮我调整更美观的格式，提前抱歉 > 如果各位对于本项目有任何的建议或者想法，可以随时私信我或者提 issue ，第一次写这种项目，请各位多多包容 我之前在自己做梯子的时候，老是需要在好几个 ssh 里面跳来跳去，有时候还会输入指令给错的服务器，每次让 ai 做小改动，都要给他说每台服务器的基本情况。但是现在找到的 mcp 服务又大多是单台服务器，不是跨服务器的。 所以我就写了 Flotilla 这个项目：一个把整个服务器舰队当成一个整体来管理的 MCP Server 。 ![image]( https://mac-dropbox.s3.bitiful.net/0-banner.png?no-wait=on) ### 我想先讲讲在我实际使用中它解决了我的什么问题 1. 只需要和 agent 说一句话，他就会自动获取我所有服务器的状态，他们之间的联系 2. 我让 ai 帮我做一个线路+落地的节点，全部不需要我在两台服务器操作，它自动在两台服务器执行需要的命令 3. 让他获取我们所有服务的 nginx 状态和情况，可以直接做出一个网络拓扑图 ![image]( https://mac-dropbox.s3.bitiful.net/3-exec-picker.png?no-wait=on) ### 安装与运行模式 做 Flotilla 的初衷就是因为我不想在多台服务器之间跳来跳去——所以安装被压缩到一句命令： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paipaiio/flotilla-mcp/main/deploy/bootstrap.sh -o bootstrap.sh bash bootstrap.sh ``` 脚本自动识别系统环境（有 Docker 用 Docker ，有 Node ≥ 20 用 Node ，都没有就自动装 Docker ），然后引导入网第一台机器、生成 token 、拉起服务——空白服务器到上线约 10 分钟。重复执行是安全的：续走未完成的部分，不重复建容器/服务。 #### 模式一：本地运行 装在自己的 MacBook 或者工作机上，本地以 stdio 暴露 MCP ，接进 Claude Code 、Cursor 等 harness： ```bash claude mcp add --transport stdio flotilla -- flotilla-mcp ``` 私钥和配置只存在你自己的机器上，信任边界最清晰；和 Claude Code 本地体验无缝——审批弹窗、交互式确认全可用。 #### 模式二：网站模式（团队 / 云端 agent ） 部署到一台服务器，把整个舰队暴露为一个带 token 鉴权的 HTTPS MCP 端点。两个典型接法： - **网站连接器**：Grok 等平台的自定义 MCP 连接器，直接填 URL + token - **聚合服务**：Cloudflare 这类 MCP 聚合/代理服务背后挂它 ```bash bash bootstrap.sh # 同一脚本；装完把 127.0.0.1:PORT 反代到 Caddy/nginx （模板见 deploy/） ``` fleet 随即成为 `https://mcp.example.com/mcp`。团队新机器入网只需一行 `join.sh --token `，人和 agent 走同一个入口，同一套策略与审计。 附图： ![image]( https://mac-dropbox.s3.bitiful.net/2-dashboard.png?no-wait=on) ![image]( https://mac-dropbox.s3.bitiful.net/4-enroll.png?no-wait=on) ![image]( https://mac-dropbox.s3.bitiful.net/3-exec-rolling.png?no-wait=on)

projects.title: bbhouse-qt, 基于 qt/qml 的跨平台 B 站客户端, 四年续作
projects.author: seelight
projects.summary: ![banner]( https://cos.endcloud.cn/v2ex/Xnip2026-09-19_14-40-19.png?imageMogr2/format/webp/thumbnail/!50p) ## [bbhouse-tauri]( https://www.v2ex.com/t/872704) 的精神续作, GPLv3 开源, [地址点这里]( https://github.com/endcloud/bbhouse-tauri-qt) ## 名字与契机 BBHouse, 取自经常能看见的"在 B 站买房"的评论. 源于个人是仓鼠党, 收藏爱好者, 对推荐流的抵抗为负; 外加关注了 3000+up 主, 无力审阅动态. 四年前的 tauri 版本有无法解决的问题: 杜比视界/低效的 IPC; WinUI 版本在 Windows 上性能问题都很大; SwiftUI 的 Vibe 效果实在不太好. 作为一个 Native 爱好者, 最终决定了 qt 版本, 解决所有问题. ## 已实现的功能 播放器: 播放列表, 杜比视界与 HDR 支持, 帧截图, 弹幕, 字幕, 倍速, 下载; 在线功能: (已关注的)动态与直播, 追番(港澳台), 流行, 特别关注; 历史记录, 稍后再看 请注意: ***无法会普通会员提供超过权限的功能*** ## feature 1. 极简, 以动态流为首页, 默认不展示 b 博, 没有推荐流 2. 动态流支持筛选 by 标题, up 主, 分区, 方便关注爆满的朋友 3. 单独生命周期的播放窗口与列表, 基于 mpv 后端, 支持杜比视界与 HDR 4. 对随机出现的 PCDN 进行了降权处理 5. 支持代理播放港澳台番剧 6. 完善的下载管理与本地导入弹幕播放功能 7. 现代化的 FluentUI, 明/暗, 多语言支持. 8. 高性能的 Native 应用, 采用全国***最小而美的 app(微信)***同源技术, qt+cpp 构建二进制 9. 跨平台(目前 release: Windows_x64, macOS_arm64) 10. 基于 cookie 认证, 轻依赖 ## 特色功能 1. 本地特别关注: 解决特别关注有上限的问题, 方便查看 UP 主空间, 追更 2. 本地历史缓存: 定期同步, 解决云历史有上限的问题 ## todo - 评论区 - AI 分析与推荐 - mpv 的 shader 插件, 如 anime4K ## vibe 声明 1. 本项目由于需要 FluentUI, port 自 WinUI 版本的同名项目与, port 时同步参考了原先的 taur 项目, 此过程使用 `Zcode GLM-5.3-flash` 完成 2. 多平台编译构建排错, 此过程使用 `Trae Kimi-K3` 完成 3. 细节与优化以及后续, 此过程使用 `Codex GPT-6-Astra` 完成 ## 致谢 ### mpv 后端的接入 - [Bili.Copilot]( https://github.com/Richasy/Bili.Copilot) - [wiliwili]( https://github.com/xfangfang/wiliwili) ### 弹幕实现与优化 - [DanmakuFrostMaster]( https://github.com/cotaku/DanmakuFrostMaster) - [Danmaku]( https://github.com/weizhenye/Danmaku) - [biliLocal]( https://github.com/ancientlysine/bililocal) - [pakku.js]( https://github.com/xmcp/pakku.js) ### 在线服务 - [bilibili-api-collect]() - [哔哩哔哩-干杯]( https://www.bilibili.com/space) ### 其他 - 向所有曾留言/star/pr 的 V 友致谢, 22 年的这个项目, 对我个人而言, 在工作和生活中, 都带来了莫大鼓励. ## 尾声 碎碎念 AI 四年前的[bbhouse-tauri](), 开发时间 2 周, 只有 1/10 的模板 ts 是 copilot 生成的, 当时我甚至为 copilot 能自动识别 macOS/Windows 的不同 path 而兴奋; 今年的[bbhouse-qt](), 开发时间 3 天, 算上 port 和走的弯路, 也是两周, 全程由 harness+LLM 接管, 哪怕最后接入的 Astra 也只是让我"有些兴奋". 今年四月我退订了续费 5 年的 copilot, 然后是中转站和各种 plan. 至少到目前为止, 我还是很兴奋, 工作也还在, 只是项目变大了, 变多了:) 希望大家与 AI 都能有一个美好的未来. ## 实机截图 ![动态]( https://cos.endcloud.cn/v2ex/Xnip2026-09-19_14-40-42.png?imageMogr2/format/webp/thumbnail/!50p) ![流行]( https://cos.endcloud.cn/v2ex/Xnip2026-09-19_14-40-52.png?imageMogr2/format/webp/thumbnail/!50p) ![直播]( https://cos.endcloud.cn/v2ex/Xnip2026-09-19_14-40-32.png?imageMogr2/format/webp/thumbnail/!50p) ![番剧-港澳台]( https://cos.endcloud.cn/v2ex/Xnip2026-09-19_14-45-06.png?imageMogr2/format/webp/thumbnail/!50p) ![特别关注]( https://cos.endcloud.cn/v2ex/Xnip2026-09-19_14-41-05.png?imageMogr2/format/webp/thumbnail/!50p) ![本地历史缓存]( https://cos.endcloud.cn/v2ex/Xnip2026-09-19_14-42-11.png?imageMogr2/format/webp/thumbnail/!50p) ![播放器]( https://cos.endcloud.cn/v2ex/Xnip2026-09-19_14-46-09.png?imageMogr2/format/webp/thumbnail/!50p)

projects.author: Fhaxikii

github.description: Nano-Lumen is resident general-purpose agent for Windows desktop, designed as a persistent-state system: cross-session, crash-recoverable, local-first privacy. (Beta)

projects.summary: GitHub License：Apache-2.0 预览（终端风主题） 解决了什么痛点？ 现在的 AI Agent 几乎都一个样：开会话 → 丢目标 → 干完走人。历史、状态、生命周期全塞在一个 session 对象里： 同一 session 下上下文长期经过多次压缩后，最终会导致水位逐渐抬高，直到提示 session 不可用，聊了很久的对话说没就没了； 你说"我刚改的那个文件"，它不知道，因为它并不能实时感知到你； 它能不能做一件事，完全取决于预先内置了多少工具/MCP，AI的能力边界取决于已有的工具集合。 核心功能与特色 1. 没有 Session，只有 Task：状态所有权、对话历史、上下文管理、长期记忆是四个独立系统，压缩上下文、崩溃都不会失忆； 2. 轨迹感知：它持续观测你在哪个窗口、改了什么文件、停了多久。你说"继续刚才那个"，它接得上，不用你解释； 3. 目标导向，不是工具驱动：任务超出内置工具时，它先判断能否临时写段脚本直接跑，或者也能将脚本变成长期可用的内置插件；也不行？就自己去 MCP 生态里找——查官方 Registry、翻 GitHub / HuggingFace 做工程尽调，验证通过才接进来。它的上限不是你预装了多少，而是整个互联网有什么； 4. 操作系统：GUI 操作按风险分级，危险命令有独立第三方分类器兜底；检测到你动鼠标键盘立刻让出前台，不假设用户本人不中途操作；每一次 OS 动作都留痕； 5. 上下文治理：长对话按新鲜度分层压缩，永不爆上下文，也永远不会"会话已过期"。 技术实现与亮点 截止目前开发期五个月左右、约 9 万行有效代码（含测试，测试套件随仓库分发），单进程 Windows 桌面应用，Apache-2.0； 状态机内核：所有状态变更走唯一 write entry，重启后从持久化状态自动收敛，崩溃/任务当中关闭等情况下，下次启动还能问你要不要继续； 上下文逐级衰减，是渐进压缩而不是粗暴截断； 本地离线 RAG（bge-m3 嵌入 + 向量召回），无云上传； ...... 目前是 Beta —— 欢迎来读源码、提 issue、改代码。

projects.summary: 目前大多数 Agent Skills 是给程序员写代码用的。这个仓库里的 18 个 skill 面向做决策、做研究、写文档的人：设计思维、批判性思考、根因分析、市场调研、战略分析、数据分析、长文档精读、Diataxis 文档写作、演示文稿等。 我是越南的开发者，这些 skill 最初都是为自己的工作写的，现在仍在日常使用。 特点 每个 skill 是一套带步骤和检查点的方法。以 design-thinking 为例：每条洞察必须能追溯到登记过的证据来源，没有来源的结论会一直标注为"假设"；到了用户访谈环节，agent 会停下来等你去做真实访谈，不会编造用户画像和引语。 deep-reader 用于精读 50 页以上的书、论文或学位论文，不需要把全文塞进上下文，并保留带页码的笔记，下次可以接着提问。 遵循 agentskills.io 的 SKILL.md 规范。我自己在 Claude 和 DeepSeek 模型上实际使用过；Qwen Code、Kimi CLI、Trae 等工具也支持该规范，但我还没有逐一测试，欢迎反馈。 MIT 协议；仓库和每个 skill 都有中文 README。 安装 bash npx skills add tronghieu/agent-skills 只装一个 npx skills add tronghieu/agent-skills --skill deep-reader 如果访问 GitHub 较慢，skills/ 目录下每个 skill 都有对应的 zip 包，下载后解压到 ~/.claude/skills/ 或 ~/.agents/skills/ 即可。

projects.summary: Hi hacker news, I am Kaushal, founder of echowin and also the guy creating TurnPanel. It began as an internally developed tool because my team and I were so sick of having to constantly bounce context around between ai chats, coding agents engines terminals, browsers files scripts, TurnPanel is a local-first workspace in which an agent can operate throughout your computer, orchestrate other agents and tools, and preserve valuable context over time. Its background maintenance processes transform commonly-used knowledge and tasks into reusable memories and skills stored locally - that's what I mean by self-evolving: it becomes more helpful through tasks finished, but cannot change its own permissions. It further includes a visible browser with DOM and CDP access, and it does a benchmark of your machine to suggest and set up appropriate local models. You may alternatively connect to codex openrouter opencode or another openai compatible provider, change models between different jobs, and run different models for helper agents. It is capable of monitoring conversational harnesses like kod and codex, keeping their terminals displayed, and responding to simple queries based on pre-existing contextual information in the workspace. Also, for constructing persistent dashboard track review queues, and other small utilities, the mini-app SDK is available that eliminate the need of creating a new project and deploying stack. Spaces form a safety boundary by taking care of what memories files services, browser sessions, models, and actions are accessible to each job, and agents are not able to add capacity to the grants. Logins payment destructive actions, and follow-up confirmations hand control back to the user. Complete workspace like jobs terminals browser streams, applications, and long-run processes can also be used via browser or PWA remotely. Its in public beta for mac and PC, with linux in the works. The basic local version is free, pro adds remote access and higher hosted-service limits. I'll be available to answer questions on how it works.

projects.title: Show HN: Microsoft Office running with Wine on Linux with no virtualization
projects.author: tombert

github.name: Tombert/office365_flake
github.description: A set of Nix Flakes and scripts to get Office 365 working on Linux without virtualization.

projects.summary: Microsoft Office famously hasn't worked well with Wine since Office 2007. There are lots of solutions out there to work around this, but all of them involve fairly heavy virtualization. Multiple people have told me that their biggest hangup for switching to Linux from Windows is the lack of the desktop version of Microsoft Office, and they don't want to run a VM to get around it. I recently fell into a bunch of free time with a Claude Max subscription, so I got Fable to hack at this until it worked! And with this, we have Microsoft Office running on Linux, with no Windows in sight! I can't promise that this will work on everyone's computer, but I did put this all in Nix Flakes, so ideally it should be relatively reproducible on any Linux system with the Nix package manager and Flakes enabled. Also, it does not work very well with X, but Wayland appears to work fine. This is not warez. You need a valid license for Office 365 for this to work. You also need to register on Microsoft's website in a browser ; the flow for registering in the app proved to be tricky and not worth pursuing. This is more proof of concept than anything else; I have no doubt that there are bugs and improvements to be made. I have only tested this with NixOS on Sway and KDE, and as stated it only really works with Wayland and the absolute latest GE-Proton, but I believe it would work fine with Gnome or any other Wayland desktop. Full disclosure, Claude Code with Fable did the vast vast majority of the work on this. I ended up primarily just reading log messages and complaining back to it.

projects.summary: I wanted to manage long horizon agentic workstreams via voice, then put my phone down, and have a harness manage completion - extending into full computer use. I was trying to build a personal Jarvis, so I benchmarked AutoBot to see how close I could get: - OSWorld: 32.41% (moved Sol Max from 4th to 1st, beating Opus 5) - AssistantBench: 50.70% Hermes and OpenClaw, but without needing a weekend and VMs. And with the ability to manage deep personalization AND keep strict privacy rules, storing data on encrypted disk. AutoBot is a passion project that grew out of trying to make this all work for myself. I’m sharing it here because I suspect other here have the same frustration. And I’m curious what else everyone is doing for this. It’s an MIT-licensed harness that lives within a project. Native voice lets me discuss tasks, check progress, and steer work; a local ledger tracks unfinished outputs and the evidence needed to call them done. Memory drives more autonomy over time, and defrags and locks in learning nightly while a heartbeat system persists execution. I’m not selling anything. projects.title: [开源自荐] dsh-novel-craft：把作者的点选压成写作规律，只有规律进模型上下文
projects.author: shiyan688

github.name: shiyan688/dsh-novel-craft
github.description: 禁AI腔清单能让模型不像 AI，这个工作台让它像你：标好/坏段落 → 压成写作规律（只有规律进写稿上下文）→ 开新章（方向/候选/选段/合并定稿）→ 批注式微调（只改你标过的段，逐字核对）→ 张力曲线与账目体检。dsh 插件，775 条断言。

projects.summary: 安装：dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-novel-craft（npm dsh-novel-craft@0.1.4，MIT） 这是什么 给中文网文/小说创作场景做的一个「作者品味校准」工作台，是 DeepSeek Harness 的插件（宿主半区 + 浏览器半区）。 一句话：一轮生成若干"结构不同"的候选稿，作者只做一件事——在觉得好的段落上点一下、在别扭的段落上点一下。这些点选被压成可复用的写作规律，下一轮写稿照着收敛。 我遇到的问题（自己写了半年小说，都是真事） 1. 禁AI腔清单能让模型不像 AI，但做不到"像这个作者"。 清单人人都在抄，抄完模型不油腻了，可它依然不是我。 2. 作者的真实反馈从来不沉淀。 今天说"太刻意"，明天说"没网感"，第三轮同一个毛病。因为我给的是评价，不是可复用的写法。 3. 原文喂不进上下文。 那把作者选中的段落整理成档案交给模型？起步 6 KB，一轮一个样，模型还得自己从原文里猜规律——猜不准，还烧掉上下文预算。 做法：三层分离，加一条硬规则 硬规则是：进模型上下文的只有规律，原文永远不进。 | 文件（都在 <候选目录>/.dsh-novel-craft/） | 给谁看 | 进上下文？ | | --- | --- | --- | | marks.json | 工作台（机器可读的好/坏标注） | ❌ 永不 | | 证据摘录.md | 原文证据，给人回查、给提炼当输入 | ❌（文件头写着"不要读进写稿上下文"） | | 作者偏好档案.md | 写稿会话只读这一份（只有规律） | ✅ 就它 | 真机数字（不是估算） 在一份真实书稿上点 30 段好/坏（第 1、2、8 章） 点一次「提炼规律」：1.8 秒回来 14 条规律 作者偏好档案.md 从 6140 B 的原文摘录变成 714 B 的规律，里面一条原文都没有 下一轮写稿只需要读这 714 B 提炼出来的规律长这样（原样抄几条）： 喜欢： 器物先动，人后发声，用声响顶点收束静默 给反派一句极短的私人恐惧，落点在赔不起 避免： 不要用比喻堆砌写人群的恐惧 不要用旁白解释反应者的心理活动 规律是怎么来的（以及为什么不是全自动） 一次便宜的辅助模型调用把待提炼的原文压成条目，但条目不直接进档案——作者逐条勾选才采纳，水位随之前移，同一段不会被重复送。规律区是作者的，工作台维护的自动块之外永不被覆盖，单条规律可以一键删掉。 顺手记两个插件坑（可能对写 dsh 插件的人有用） 1. 插件行的 apply 可能早于服务挂载：在 0.1.6-alpha.1 上实测，同步 apply 里 ctx.get('webServer') 拿到的是 undefined——写成"取不到就 return"的插件会在新版本上静默什么都不做。改成 ctx.inject(['settings','webServer'], …) 等就绪（带超时兜底）即可。 2. 调模型做结构化输出要默认关掉推理：推理 token 和正文共用一份输出预算，我这边表现是"接口 5.6 秒返回、解析出 0 条规律"，关掉推理 + 抬高预算后 1.8 秒出 14 条（官方 Discussion #6857 也写了这条）。 3. 另外客户端 bundle 的下发地址从 /plugins/<id>/client.js 变成了组合脚本 /plugins/??a/client.js,b/client.js&rev=…——插件不用管，但拿裸 URL 做测试的人会误以为"插件没被收录"。 工程质量 209 项断言：静态守卫（Hook 顺序、词条完整性）+ 回环端口上的接口闭环（含假 LLM 的提炼链路）+ 用成对 react/react-dom 把客户端组件真渲染成 HTML；测试不依赖任何本机路径 scripts/check-dsh-compat.mjs + CI 矩阵：每周自动在 latest / next / alpha / 0.1.2-rc.1 四档上真装一份 dsh、起服务、验宿主路由与客户端半区下发 出处与致谢：skills/novel-writing 的禁AI腔清单改编自 dsh-novel-solo（MIT），平台 DeepSeek Harness（MIT），完整声明在 THIRDPARTYNOTICES.md 仓库里还带了两个配套 skill（taste-calibration / novel-writing），装到 .dsh/skills/ 即可，插件负责"让你低负担地点"，skill 负责"告诉 agent 怎么用这些标注"。

projects.summary: DatI(Data Intelligence) 是连接 AI Agent 与企业数据库 的轻量级语义网关 —— 仅需接入数据库、配置语义信息、按需启用预置工具与参数化 SQL 工具，即可发布 MCP 服务，灵活地接入用户的 Agent 或任意 MCP Host 适用场景 智能问数：接入业务数据库，通过业务元数据配置以及通用预置工具即可支持 NL2SQL 分析工作流 轻应用搭建：将数据库封装为 MCP 服务，Agent 通过对话即可直接对业务数据增删改查，快速构建轻量级应用 亮点 1. 多数据库：支持 MySQL、PostgreSQL、ClickHouse、Doris 等多种关系型与分析型数据库 2. 语义增强：支持业务术语、字段别名与枚举字典值自动抽取，结合语义检索，让模型能够理解业务黑话、快速找对表 3. 灵活集成：基于标准 MCP 协议（Streamable HTTP），灵活集成至用户现有 Agent 或工作流 4. 高效构建：提供开箱即用的预置工具（元数据探查、SQL 执行）与参数化 SQL 工具，免部署发布 MCP 服务 5. 安全管控：凭据集中托管，支持按用户权限隔离 当前的独立ChatBI不能集成到用户自己工作流（例如洞察完数据后可能要输出汇报材料或者下发任务）；而标准数据库MCP/Skill 缺少语义配置与权限管控

projects.title: [开源自荐] tool-bridge: Agent 的触手, 连接 设备/Context/MCP. 支持反向注册, SDK...
projects.author: Disdjj
projects.summary: 先上链接: 官方文档: 过去一年在一些AI Starup 工作, 在这些强调 AI Native 的公司中做 Agent Infra 的过程中, 经常会遇到一些问题: 1. 大量的不同业务的 Agent 希望能够共享工具, 但是也希望有足够的限制(某些工具禁止访问) 2. 希望 Agent 和 Agent 之间能够共享 Context, 用飞书cli 太重, 而且 agent 创建的文档访问权限控制很麻烦 3. 聚合MCP, 提供统一的开发体验, 某些 MCP 由于 Seat 限制不能够添加过多的 User 席位, 而且最好能够自部署, 没有商业风险 4. 希望能够直接让 Agent 使用某些命令排查线上的机器/Pod/服务 5. 自建的 mcp 又总是很难注册到 MCP Gateway 以上就是我在做 Agent Infra 遇到的一些问题, 分散来看, 每一个其实都有解决方案. 比如说 mcporter / mintlify / 各种 mcp gateway / agentdock ... 但是作为部署/管理/成本/维护的考虑, 把这些功能分散到 N 个服务中好像有太过于舍本逐末. 于是最近两个月, 我做了 tool-bridge, 简单来说: 基于树描述组织中的所有工具/MCP/Context/设备, 提供类似 cli 的 help 语义 + agent自主的 feedback + SDK + 支持反向注册, 实现的一套 Agent 的工具调用方式. 当然, 本身是兼容 MCP 的, 同时 tool-bridge 也支持 接入mcp, 也支持以 mcp 的方式暴露. 几个用例 目前的范围能力 tool-bridge 对开发者提供: SDK / Plugin-SDK / 完全开源的 Server / Dashboard tool-bridge 对Agent提供: API / CLI / MCP 的接入支持 tool-bridge 对设备提供: 1. linux / mac / windows 的 shell / Daemon / 自定义设备路径 的能力 2. ios / android 的通知/可离线投递的信箱/震动/闪光/摄像头调用(根据设置权限) 的能力 目前我把目前使用的 Agent 对 MCP/Context/设备 的调用都迁移到了 tool-bridge, 体验不错, 推荐使用! 欢迎 Star/Issue/PR, 目前处于 Pre-Launch 的阶段, API UI CMD 可能会有变更, 但是会尽快推出 1.0 的 Stable-Release

projects.title: Show HN: Blue – open-source governance for coding agents
projects.author: tomislavs
projects.summary: Hey HN, After migrating to an inference gateway to serve internal usage across an organization, problems have started to pop up. Once you detach from a managed ecosystem such as OpenAI or Anthropic you lose governance capabilities that makes the transition difficult. - Losing access to a central plugin hub for delivering MCPs, skills, etc. A gateway can sort of do this but has low compatibility beyond skills, different harnesses, and version ranges - Inability to deliver managed config (model defaults, etc). Can sort of be done with MDM/Jamf but doesn't reach contractors and doesn't follow employees to other machines - Gateway configuration is awkward for devs transitioning from SSO and API keys sit in plain text on their machines The gateway transition facilitates new model families (Kimi, Deepseek, etc) which are best utilized with new harnesses beyond Codex or Claude Code. Managing these additional tools multiplies the governance problems. Lastly, attempting to deliver an attribution program which can tag inference requests with ticket numbers and other metadata to facilitate Opex/Capex calcs for finance becomes fairly unfeasible when there are multiple harnesses across arbitrary versions. This was not solved with managed ecosystems either to be fair, but requires some self-serve program or some local MITM proxy which is a distribution and versioning problem in of itself. I built Blue to attempt to solve these problems. It's an MIT open source, self-hostable control plane. Developers install a universal CLI and point it at their hosted control plane tenant. On launch, it reconciles the organization's policy per harness, delivers extensions, and configures the gateway. It then launches and passes control to the native CLI (Kimi, OpenCode, Codex, etc) that devs already use. Authentication is via browser device authorization which mints ephemeral bearer tokens. For gateway access, these tokens are exchanged at the inference proxy (part of the self-hosted Blue image) for the real API keys. This means that devs don't need to manage API keys or even log into the gateway at all. Lastly, SCIM and OIDC are supported out of the box, so orgs can connect their identity solution immediately. Curious to hear your thoughts and if you have/solved this problem. I believe it can also be solved to some degree with a harness like Pi or even OpenCode, but that of course depends on the entire org migrating to those. Last thing I'll say is nowadays a CLI isn't enough since I've seen over 80% of devs prefer desktop apps like the ChatGPT app. We're also working on an open source desktop app that supports metaharnesses like Blue to make this transition easier. Thanks!

projects.title: 我们做了一门让 Agent 写视频的语言
projects.author: Daniel6606
projects.summary: 大家好啊，最近我们在做 Hypit： 这是一个视频描述语言，我们起名叫 SVML （ Semantic Video Markup Language ） 我们希望 Claude Code 、Codex 这样的 Agent ，能用它描述一支视频，再交给系统生成素材、处理字幕、编排画面，最后渲染成片。 项目链接： https://github.com/hypit-ai/hypit ## 从一个很具体的剪辑问题开始 我们之前给一些 AI 公司做内容，经常会参考别人做得不错的广告，再结合自己的产品重新制作 一条二十几秒的视频，要拆脚本、生成镜头、配音、剪辑、加字幕，还要安排产品特写和各种动效。即使模型已经把素材生成出来，后面依然有不少制作工作，如果你做过这件事情，你一定会知道我在说什么 其中有一件事一直让我们觉得很绕啊 写脚本的时候，我经常会边写边在脑子里构思稿子和视频的配合，比如： > 主持人说到产品名，就弹出产品卡片 > 说到“第一名”，排行榜对应的位置就亮起来 但此时还不知道这些词会落在第几秒，于是只能等语音和视频生成完，再一帧一帧地找位置，把效果对上 如果换一版台词或者只是语速变了，就得重新处理这些对应关系 所以我们想让 Agent 能直接写下这种要求，由系统根据实际素材算出时间，这个想法后来成了 SVML 里很核心的一部分：把画面效果绑定到叙事中的词 ## 视频的源文件可以长什么样 下面是一段真实的.svml 语言+视频的 demo ![]( https://i.imgur.com/AMCcmgR.gif) 把 GIF 中的案例简化 ⬇️ ``` 我会把它加进 @lifestyle 咖啡、奶昔，甚至煮意面的水里。 你这是把它当 @/lifestyle 面粉用了吧。 ``` daily-creatine 是段落名称，GIRL 和 GUY 标明每句话由谁说。 @lifestyle 和 @/lifestyle 划出了一段跨越两位说话人的语义区间。补充画面可以绑定到这段区间，覆盖相应的对话。 实际案例中的画面组件，就是通过 during={story.selection.lifestyle} 引用这段范围。 (查看完整播客源码: https://github.com/hypit-ai/hypit/blob/main/examples/podcast/reference.svml) 这些标记本身只描述位置，具体显示什么，由引用它们的组件决定。素材生成后，系统通过语音对齐，把这些位置映射到实际时间。改台词或换语言时，重新生成、对齐相关素材，画面就能按新的时间定位。 完整的语法说明在： https://hypit.ai/quickstart/script/ ## 复刻视频，是这门语言的一个入口 现在最容易体验 Hypit 的方式，是给 Agent 一条参考视频，让它把里面的画面、台词、字幕和特效关系重建成 workflow ![]( https://i.imgur.com/rNe3HKa.gif) 可以看这个街头采访的案例：同一套结构，可以把主持人换成，被采访者换成动漫人物，F1 赛车手等 做出第一个版本后，源文件可以继续改: 换产品、换开场、换语言，批量生成 100 个变体，都可以围绕已有流程来做；需要重新生成的素材仍然会产生相应成本 当然，也可以没有参考视频。直接描述要做什么，由 Agent 从零组织组件和编写源文件。字幕、动效和代码渲染画面这类流程，也可以不调用生成模型。 ## 怎么用 Hypit 给 Claude Code ，Codex ，或者 Hermes 安装 skills 先： ``` npx skills add hypit-ai/hypit -g ``` 然后提供一条参考视频： ``` /hypit 复刻这个视频: /path/to/video.mp4 ``` 首次使用时，Agent 会检查并协助准备运行环境。你可以继续告诉它要改什么，检查制作方案、确认所需服务和费用，再生成成片。上手文档 Hypit 本身免费，不收席位费和按次渲染费；付费模型 API 和 Agent 的费用另算，平均制作一个视频的 API 成本，换算下来在 1 美金左右！ 欢迎大家来提提建议

projects.title: [开源自荐] llmdoc: 一个经过实践考验的 codebase memory 方案
projects.author: Disdjj
projects.summary: llmdoc首页: 标题的说明 标题的实践考验指的是在两个 AI Starup 公司的实践, 支撑了大约 3 亿 ARR 产品的迭代(其实应该是 2.9 亿 ARR, 四舍五入其实差不多, 当然了其实是两家公司的两家产品加起来的 ARR 😭) 在前司主要负责公司的 AI/Agent 建设, 同时也比较深入的参与了业务的开发, 一些开发上的尤其是 人&人, 人&AI 的协作的痛点感知还是非常清晰的. 我相信我列出的问题肯定不止一个人遇到过: 1. AI 写的代码没有沿用默认的技术框架/方案 2. 需要在 Coding 前不断地输入/纠正 3. 已经有的解决方案/函数/包库没有直接用, 又造了一堆轮子 4. 明明纠正过很多次, 同样的错误在下一次又犯病 5. 使用的 memory 没有版本化管理, 代码回滚/合并了, memory 没有更新 6. 给了目标之后, 用了巨多时间巨多 context, 读取了N 多文件, 问了 N 个问题, 然后在过了甜点 context 阈值的情况下开始工作, 写的乱七八糟 context floor 我曾经给很多人表达过一个观点: Agent 完成工作的好坏, 取决于 context 的丰富程度 这里有几个需要说明的地方: 1. 工作的好坏: 这里是靠人判断的, 架构是否合理, 抽象是否清晰, 是不是没有重复造轮子... 2. Context 的丰富程度: 这里指的是和"完成目标"相关的 Context, 尽可能的多而且不重复, 在 context 无限大, 甜点 window 无限长的情况下, 最好的方案是把代码库+架构+db+UI+PRD 全都塞进去 换句话说: 如果有办法能够稳定的为 Agent 提供良好的快速到达满足工作条件的 Context 路径, 就能提升 Agent 的工作效果和工作效率 context floor 只是我臆造的一个名词, 大家不用搜索, 我在一篇早期的 blog 里简单的说了一下, 大家不用关心 llmdoc 好了, 为了引出正文已经瞎扯了很多了

projects.title: 四年前做的 WebRTC 聊天室，现在可以让 Agent 进来一起干活了
projects.author: bmpidev2019
projects.summary: 之前在 V2EX 发过几次 free4.chat ，最早就是一个不用注册、打开链接就能聊的 WebRTC 语音聊天室。 上次更新还是给房间里塞了一个 AI 助手。最近又折腾了不少，现在方向有点不一样了：不再自己托管一个 AI Bot ，而是让你本来就在用的 Agent 直接进房间。 目前 Codex 、Claude 、Pi 、Hermes 、OpenCode 这些都可以作为独立参与者加入。 比如我现在实际跑过的场景： Mac mini 上跑一个 Agent ，MacBook 上跑另一个 Agent 。两个 Agent 加入同一个临时房间，可以互相发现、发任务请求、接受或拒绝，然后把文件和结果通过房间传回来。 不需要共享文件系统，也不需要把两个 Agent 放进同一个平台。 人也可以直接在浏览器房间里和 Agent 协作。现在有 Task ，可以单独和某个 Agent 干一件事，发图片/文件，看执行状态； Agent 需要权限时可以在房间里弹审批卡；如果纯文字不太好表达，Agent 还可以临时生成一个简单的交互界面。 Agent 自己的模型、工具、代码仓库、浏览器登录状态、API Key 都还是留在自己的机器上，free4chat 只负责提供一个临时房间把它们连起来。 浏览器不是必须的，两个 Agent 也可以直接从终端建房、加入然后协作。 在线： https://free4.chat/ 开源： https://github.com/i365dev/free4chat Agent 协作文档： https://www.free4.chat/docs/guides/cross-machine-collaboration 之前的帖子： https://v2ex.com/t/828646 https://v2ex.com/t/1213306 最近基本把这个项目当 Agent 协作的实验田了，如果有人平时同时用 Codex / Claude / Pi 之类的，可以试试看这种“临时拉进一个房间干活”的方式有没有实际用途。

projects.title: dshcloud：开源自托管的 DeepSeek Harness 多用户、多实例平台
projects.author: eskyle2001
projects.summary: 开源仓库地址： https://github.com/eskim2001/dshcloud 自托管的多用户、多实例平台，用户数据持久化 ## 起源 最近用 dsh 创造模式用的很多，经常就把 dsh 改造成一个完全不同的 app 了，这时候要分享给不太会用的朋友比较麻烦，就想到了把这个部署到云上。没考虑现有的方案主要是第二个问题，dsh 版本更新的很快，希望能方便的更新 dsh ，保留原来的用户数据，于是就想到了做容器化的隔离+mount 持久化。 **什么时候用得上** - 和朋友分享你改造的 dsh：每个 dsh 是一个独立域名 ，数据与配额互相隔离，甚至未来可以作为多租户 - 不想依赖本地设备：跑在自己的 VPS 上持续在线，浏览器从任意设备进 - 想要快速升级新版的 dsh：换镜像升级，升前自动打数据快照，失败能回滚 **具体能力** - workspace 创建/启停/重建/删除：每个 workspace 独立容器 + 持久化存储，CPU 、内存、进程数、磁盘容量都有配额 - 邀请制多用户：管理员发邀请链接加人，没有公开注册 - 访问控制：workspace 端口只绑宿主机回环，外部访问要走 Traefik forward-auth + 归属校验 + 按 workspace 的签名校验 - 版本管理：从 GHCR 同步版本目录、发布稳定版本、配置默认版本 - 控制台：配额查看、用量采样、workspace 日志流 - 界面支持中英文、明暗主题、⌘K 命令菜单 **先在线试试** 在线 demo： https://console.demo.dshcloud.app demo-user 这个 workspace 放了一个 10 块钱的 key ，可以直接测试 现在比较有意思的是这样的，你可以和你的朋友一起用一个账号登录同一个实例，dsh 支持两边都事实更新，这个就有点像一些协作文档一样了，甚至你俩可以在同一个实例里面用 AI 对战之类的，后续会考虑单独做 dsh 的分享功能，现在必须要同一个账号才行 **装在自己服务器上** 需要一台 Linux + Docker Compose （本地用 mac 也可以），放开 80/443 端口，预留磁盘配额： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eskim2001/dshcloud/main/scripts/install.sh | bash ``` **当前状态**：早期开发。可用于评估和开发，打算暴露到公网的话。 有兴趣的点 star ，这里或者 issue 有任何反馈（包括吐槽）都欢迎。

projects.title: Show HN: Agenttik – work on multiple projects in parallel with AI agents
projects.author: psanchez
projects.summary: Hi! I've been reading HN daily for almost 16 years. Really glad this community exist. This is my first Show HN, so I hope you find this tool useful/interesting. During my summer holidays I started playing with latest AI models on personal projects. At one point I started working in parallel with the same project and tried different approaches. The one that worked best for me was to clone the repo and distribute work among different AI workers, work in parallel but with different branches & folders. This allowed me to review and merge work afterwards. The thing is, spawning several agents in parallel was challenging. I could work on multiple features and bugfix at once, but it was hard to keep track what I was working on. I was jumping from one thing to another, and back; from one window to another. Switching tasks like this was mentally exhausting. Holidays were over, and after returning to my day to day work, I continued working using a similar approach not on one, but also on multiple projects, but I still could not find how to work in a more organized way without the mental toll. This space is growing really fast, and I haven't been able to find the right tool for myself, so I decided to build my own. I wanted a tool that would help me manage multiple projects at once, work with multiple agents, even from different providers, where I could chose between my personal and work subscriptions depending on the project, where I could easily review changes without leaving the tool if I wanted, or go all in and delegate fully to agents; one where I had quick shortcuts to move around, where I could schedule work or enqueue work for later so agents could work on one task after another. agenttik is my way of tackling this problem to work on multiple projects in parallel, while allowing myself to be on the driver seat. I can give as much autonomy as I want to the agents while keeping things organized in my head. I've been hesitating for hours on whether to submit or not, but hey "if you are not ashamed of your project, you are shipping too late" Honestly, this project has exactly one week of development, started from scratch, and even though it is still early on, it has been extremely useful for me. I've built in a week things that would have taken me months, not only built the tool itself but other projects as well (most of the merit is still on the models used, but would have had no way of distributing all the work, though). Feel free to try. Here's how I would get started: - Open a project you already have - Add some general prompt (in the project area) or add to your AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (to instruct it to do regular commits and/or work with branches, and also instructions on how to build effective tests so that it can self-correct). - Chose your subscriptin of choice: Claude Code / Open AI subscription / ... - Pick big models (Opus High to Max / Fable Medium to Max / Astra Medium to Max) for bigger autonomy and try not to do hand-holding Finally, start sending/enqueuing tasks on all the features you want your product to have, bugfixes, ... use a new prompt per task (Ctrl+T / Cmd+T), I recommend using big models to avoid investing your own time reviewing, and then once LLM is done, review and archive that task or continue iterating. Keep adding tasks as you think on them. Add more projects as you start feeling comfortable. It has been really addictive for me to see the speed of development when working like this. I got totally hooked. Speed of iteration is insane. Happy to discuss any feedback you have even if it is about other tools or ways of working with AI these days! I hope you like it!!

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Flashgate：让 AI 编程 agent 不敢谎报固件能跑的硬件验证门禁
projects.author: Lion-1209

github.name: Lion-1209/flashgate
github.description: The agent can't claim the firmware works — until the board says so. Hardware-in-the-loop verification gate: build → flash → boot banner → exit code.

projects.summary: 我是 Flashgate 的维护者，自荐这个 MIT 开源的硬件在环验证工具。 AI 编程 agent 改完固件经常直接宣布"能跑了"——但它其实无从知道板子上的真实情况，编译通过不等于板子能启动。Flashgate 把最后一环交给硬件裁决： 完整验证链：编译 → ST-Link/OpenOCD 烧录 → 等板子自报身份（串口 banner 带 git sha，或 64 字节 SWD RAM 签名，后者不需要串口线）→ 发真实控制台命令、断言硬件寄存器读回值 → 结构化退出码 Stop hook 门禁：挂进 Claude Code 后，agent 改了固件没过真机验证就想收工，会被当场拦下，并把板子的失败证词（比如"收到呼吸灯命令却回报 OFF"）喂回给 agent 定位修复 每次验证（无论成败）落一份可审计的证据记录：逐项检查结论、板子原话、产物哈希 bench-serve 可把整台实验台挂上局域网，远程 agent 通过 Arm 的 device-connect 协议发现并请求真机验证（跨机实测通过） 自带 OpenOCD 后端，不需要 ST 工具链；仓库含完整可编译的 STM32H743 示例工程（正点原子 Apollo），接线后开箱可跑 仓库里有一段完整的真实 agent 会话记录：agent 被板子拦下、读证词、定位到固件里一处"静默无操作谎言"、修复、真机通过后才放行。 Python 编写，pip install flashgate 即用，目前以 STM32 为主（适配器层本周已落地，欢迎其他芯片的档案贡献）。

projects.title: [开源自荐] termcp：让 AI Agent 操作真实交互式终端，并提供可视化管理与人工接管
projects.author: UserB1ank

github.description: termcp is an MCP server written in Go that exposes interactive programs to AI Agents as persistent SSH sessions, letting Agents continuously manage and drive them. On top of that, termcp ships a dedicated session management UI that gives you full visibility into the Agent's behavior.

projects.summary: termcp 是一个支持可视化管理的面向 AI Agent 的通用交互式终端 MCP。 现在的 Agent 很擅长执行 ls、git status、curl 这类「运行一次就结束」的命令，但遇到真正的交互式程序就比较麻烦： SSH 可能先询问密码，安装程序会在中途弹出 [Y/n]，Python REPL 需要逐行输入，vim、gdb、htop、数据库 CLI 则从头到尾都在等待下一次键盘操作。 这些程序不是一次 exec 能完成的。 termcp 的思路不是为 vim 做一个 MCP、为 gdb 再做一个 MCP、为某个数据库 CLI 再做一个 MCP，而是直接把完整的终端交互能力提供给 Agent。 只要一个工具原本能够在终端里使用，Agent 就可以尝试直接通过 termcp 操作它： Agent → MCP → termcp → PTY → 任意 CLI 因此，大量已经存在几十年的命令行工具，不需要为了 AI 再重新包装一遍 API 或 MCP Server。 特点 1. 真正的交互式终端 termcp 底层使用真实 PTY。 Agent 可以读取终端输出、向 stdin 输入文本，也可以发送 Enter、Tab、Esc、Ctrl+C 等按键，然后继续读取新的输出。 也就是说，它可以像人一样不断执行： 观察 → 判断 → 输入 → 再观察 vim、gdb、htop、Python REPL、交互式安装器等程序都可以直接运行，而不是退化成一连串 bash -c。 2. Shell 会话可以跨多轮对话持续存在 Agent 启动一个程序后，不需要这一轮对话结束时把它关掉。 同一个 Shell 可以一直存在，下一轮继续操作；一条连接上还能同时打开多个 Shell，例如一个终端跑程序，另一个终端查看日志。 终端输出使用游标增量读取，不会每次都把整个历史重新塞进模型上下文。 3. 本机和远程服务器使用同一套接口 termcp 把所有终端统一成 SSH。 远程机器使用正常 SSH；本机则通过进程内嵌的 SSH Server 建立内存连接，不额外监听 TCP 端口。 因此对于 Agent 来说，本机和远程服务器没有区别。 文件操作使用 SFTP，同时支持 SSH 的本地、远程和动态端口转发。 4. 人可以实时观察并随时接管 termcp 自带 Web UI。 运行后打开： 就可以看到 Agent 正在操作的同一个终端。 vim、htop 等动态界面也会正常显示，多个终端可以像 iTerm2 一样平铺。 如果 Agent 操作错了，人可以随时直接接管键盘继续输入。 会话结束后，终端历史仍然会被保存，重启 termcp 后也可以继续查看。 5. SSH 凭据不需要交给模型 SSH 密码和私钥由 termcp 本地管理，写入后无法通过 MCP 再读取。 Agent 只需要知道一个配置名称，例如： prod-web 然后请求「连接 prod-web」即可。 主机地址、用户名、端口、密码和私钥都不需要出现在模型上下文里。 Agent 修改 SSH 配置的能力默认也是关闭的。 快捷部署 一个二进制即可运行 termcp 使用 Go 编写，MIT 协议，提供 macOS、Linux 和 Windows 的预编译版本。 Web UI、MCP SSE 和 Streamable HTTP 共用一个端口，默认是 18765，数据保存在本地 ~/.termcp，不需要额外数据库。 Claude Code、Open WebUI 以及其他支持 MCP 的客户端都可以接入。 我们希望 termcp 做的不是「再给一个工具开发一个 MCP」，而是给 Agent 一双能够操作终端的手。 只要一个工具能在终端里运行，它就有机会直接成为 Agent 的工具。

projects.title: Show HN: Pizza Bot – An inbox for AI agents that work in the background
projects.author: jd_

github.name: pizza-bot-app/pizza-bot
github.description: A local-first inbox for long-running AI agents, built with DeepAgents and LangGraph.

projects.summary: Hi HN - long-time lurker (since 2012!), first time poster. Pizza Bot is a self-hosted desktop app for Mac, Windows, and Linux that runs AI agents in the background and exposes them through an email-like UI. Finished work shows up in Unread, and anything waiting on your approval shows up in Action. It's Apache 2.0-licensed, there's no signup and no telemetry, and you bring your own model provider: Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or a local model through Ollama. There are builds on the releases page, or you can run it from source. Pizza Bot started as an internal passion project I worked on with a small team at Amazon. The whole thing came out of my frustration at having to manually log CRM activities through a browser form. I built a simple REST API called "JoeBot" that connected to my authenticated browser session over CDP and filled out the form for me using Playwright. Then I hacked up a quick Obsidian plugin so I could trigger it from my local notes (no AI and no MCP servers involved). This caught on quickly. My fellow AWS Solutions Architect Igor Fil joined up with me, and we rebranded the project as "Pizza Bot," named after Amazon's two-pizza teams. We started seeing what other automations we could build. We found a GraphQL API we could query and hacked up some "recipes" to pull data out of the CRM to help with meeting prep. That worked great, and it was right around the time MCP servers seemed to be taking off, so we decided to expose Pizza Bot as an MCP server instead, so it would be available to AI tools through natural language. This was a decent solution for technical users, but the Account Managers who live inside our CRM system wanted something too. We decided to rebuild Pizza Bot as an Electron desktop app modeled after an email inbox, so it would be familiar to non-technical users and would run on both Mac and Windows. We also bundled internal MCP servers as OCI images and hosted them in Amazon ECR as an "addon marketplace" so users could install them with one click without having to set up Amazon developer tooling. The project took off organically and expanded outside of AWS into the wider Amazon organization globally. More than 2,000 people ended up using it for meeting prep, email drafting, Slack summaries, CRM logging, prioritizing their day, and web research. Once apps like Claude Cowork and Amazon's own Quick Desktop came out, we realized the real growth opportunity was outside of Amazon. Rather than try to rip out the Amazon-specific integrations, we rebuilt Pizza Bot once more as an open source project. We leaned on coding agents heavily, which is the only reason a team our size could pull off a full rewrite. I'm pleased to say it's finally public, and we're hoping to bring in community members and see where it goes. We'd like to do for knowledge workers what Claude Code and Codex have done for programmers. A couple of things to know up front. Most of what made Pizza Bot useful on day one inside Amazon came from that internal catalog of skills and MCP servers for Amazon's own systems, and none of it could come out with the app. So it ships thinner than the version those 2,000 people used, and building that catalog back up for tools other people actually use is where we need the most help. It's also a community project and not an AWS service, so there's no support or SLA behind it. The Windows and Linux builds aren't signed yet either. On the technical side, Pizza Bot is a server and a client. The desktop app bundles both, or you can point a client at a remote backend; personally, I self-host the server on my home network and reach it from my phone over Tailscale. The server owns the thread lifecycle and checkpoints state with DeepAgents and LangGraph, and clients rehydrate from it as needed, so you can disconnect mid-run and pick the thread back up from another client. Approval pauses outlive the session that created them and collect in an Action filter, so you can answer an hour later from a different device. The agent you talk to has a sandboxed QuickJS interpreter that can reach your filesystem only if you grant it a folder, but its main job is to delegate. Each subagent is a 1:1 mapping of a Skill, and an Activity bar shows that subagent and the tool calls it's making as it works. Memory is opt-in and stored as plain markdown files on your machine. Every tool call is explicit, including looking up a memory - we err on the side of transparency to reduce surprises. Tools come from MCP servers, and skills are ordinary SKILL.md files with a per-tool approval policy, so existing skills that don't require a code interpreter should still work. What I'd most like to hear about is where the app itself gets in your way, the kind of problem you can't fix by writing a skill or an MCP server. I'm around today to answer questions!

github.description: An open-source Agent-first Identity and Access Management (IAM) /LLM MCP & agent gateway and auth server with web UI supporting OpenClaw, MCP, OAuth, OIDC, SAML, CAS, LDAP, SCIM, WebAuthn, TOTP, MFA, Face ID, Google Workspace, Azure AD

projects.summary: Casdoor 是一个开源的身份认证与访问管理平台（IAM / SSO），Go + React 写的，Apache 2.0，14.4k star。9 月 1 日发布了 v4.0，到 9 月 9 日已经迭代到 v4.3；今年 2 月它进了 CNCF 云原生全景图（Provisioning → Security & Compliance）。 先说最有用的一条：如果你在写远程 MCP Server，鉴权这块可以不用自己做了。 MCP 规范要求远程 Server 用 OAuth 2.1 鉴权，但 Agent 客户端（Claude Code、Cursor 这些）事先根本不知道自己要向谁注册，所以动态客户端注册是绕不过去的一环。Casdoor 把这套备齐了：OAuth 2.1 + PKCE、RFC 7591 动态客户端注册（注册端点在 .well-known/openid-configuration 里公布，客户端自己能发现）、RFC 7592 客户端管理、授权同意页、JWKS 与 JWT 校验。你只要把自己 MCP Server 的 Protected Resource Metadata 指向 Casdoor，剩下的认证、同意、发 token、验 token 都不用写。 它自己也是个 MCP Server，暴露 15 个工具（user / application / permission 三类对象各一套 CRUD），Claude Code 接上去可以直接说「给这个组织加个用户」。再加上 OpenClaw 接入：Agent 运行时的 trace / metric / log 按 OTLP 推进来，落成可查的记录——身份、权限、审计连成一条线。 常规能力（这部分它做了五年）：同一份用户目录可以通过 OAuth 2.0、OIDC、SAML 2.0、CAS、LDAP、SCIM 2.0 访问，所以新写的 SPA 和只认 CAS 的老系统能共用一批账号；登录方式覆盖密码、邮箱短信验证码、WebAuthn / passkey、TOTP、Face ID，外加 Google、GitHub、Entra ID 等上百个身份源；组织、应用、登录页品牌化全在 Web 控制台改，不用改配置文件重新部署；授权规则交给 Casbin。部署就一个 Go 二进制加一个数据库，没有 JVM，没有 operator。 v4 这一轮：控制台从 Ant Design 整个换成 shadcn/ui（Vite 构建，注意静态资源路径从 build/static/{js,css} 变成了 build/assets/），登录注册页重做并修好了移动端；新增 OIDC 身份源类型；LDAP 自动同步改成只在单节点跑；支持 Redis Cluster；用户的角色和权限会标出各自由哪个组、哪个角色授予。 一条命令试： bash docker run -p 8000:8000 casbin/casdoor-all-in-one 打开 ，组织 built-in，用户名 admin，密码 123（内置 SQLite 和示例数据，仅供试用）。在线 CNCF 全景图条目：

projects.title: 【开源自荐】nautilus-compass:给 AI Agent 装上会传承、可验证的集体记忆
projects.author: chunxiaoxx

github.name: chunxiaoxx/nautilus-compass
github.description: Reliability layer for multi-agent setups — keep agents coordinating without an orchestrator. Cross-dialog contracts + drift detection + black-box memory (no LLM extraction).

projects.summary: 一个人写了 130 天的开源 agent 记忆层(Modified MIT)。它想解决的问题比「记住」再往前一步:agent 团队的集体记忆,怎么可信地传承。 架构 bet:写入时不调 LLM。会话原文 + 本地 BGE-m3,零抽取、零上云,记忆写入零 token 成本;智能全在读取侧——按问题类型路由检索单元(单会话问题只取 turn 级小块,不塞整个会话)。LongMemEval-S 全 500 题:检索 P@1 0.890 vs mem0 2.0.19 的 0.774(同题同判据,evidence 文件+复现脚本在仓库,复跑约 $3.50)。 三个别的记忆层没有的东西: 一、记忆有治理。 每条记忆写入时标注来源等级(measured / inferred / heard),查重门(BGE 三档:≥0.9 合并 / 灰区 / unique),条目间的 [[引用]] 沿链带出——记忆不是越多越好,是越可信越好。 二、组织记忆。 我家四个 AI 工作框(写代码 / 跑评测 / 管平台 / 做数据)共用这一个记忆库:项目级隔离、跨框可引用。agent A 踩过的坑封装成「记忆胶囊」,agent B 接手同任务直接绕开——有 B 从 FAIL 到 PASS 的实录。AI 团队的 onboarding,不再从零开始。 三、跑分即证据包。 对外公布的每个数字 = sha256 清单 + 字节可复算 + ed25519 签名,clone 后两条命令可验,不需要信任作者;不可复算的数字一律不进包、只做披露(判官网关静默故障把 14.2% 的题记成「答错」——这种事故我们抓过五次,全部写进协议文档)。 想象空间:当每个 agent 都带着可信的集体记忆工作,「组织」的边界就从人类扩展到人机混合体。智能 = 压缩 + 验证——压缩各家都在做,我们把验证那半,做成了基础设施。 Claude Code / Cursor / Cline 等一键接入(MCP),也有托管自助版。欢迎来验数字:推翻我们的结果,同样上墙。

projects.title: 「开源自荐」RuwoScan - 基于Agentic 框架的自动化AI漏洞扫描工具

projects.title: [开源推荐] 统一管理多个 AI 编程 Agent 会话记录的本地工具
projects.author: HarryHeYu

github.name: HarryHeYu/voyager
github.description: One searchable index across every AI coding agent on your machine — Codex, Claude Code, ZCode, DSH, Grok, Cursor, Antigravity, Kiro. Scan, search, export and resume all your agent sessions locally. No cloud, no telemetry.

projects.summary: Voyager 是一个本地 AI Coding Agent 会话管理工具，可以统一索引 Codex、Claude Code、ZCode、DSH、Grok CLI、Cursor 等工具产生的会话记录，并提供跨 Agent 全文搜索、项目时间线、自动增量同步、工作摘要、会话导出、原生恢复以及跨 Agent 上下文交接等功能。 亮点 多个 Agent，一个统一索引：支持 Codex、Claude Code、ZCode、DSH、Grok CLI、Cursor、Kiro、Antigravity 等 AI 编程工具，把原本分散在 JSONL、SQLite、zstd 等不同格式和目录中的会话统一管理。 跨 Agent 全文搜索：所有会话统一建立本地 SQLite 索引，可以直接搜索历史问题、执行过的命令、文件名和工具调用，并支持中文子串搜索。 按项目查看完整开发时间线：通过 voyager repo 可以查看同一个项目先后被哪些 Agent 操作过、什么时候操作以及做了什么，把不同 Agent 中零散的工作记录串成一条时间线。 自动增量同步：除了手动执行 voyager scan，还可以运行 voyager watch --interval 300 定时增量更新索引，并可加入系统自启动，基本无需手动维护索引。 快速回顾所有 Agent 最近在做什么：voyager brief 可以生成最近 48 小时的跨 Agent 工作摘要，方便快速回顾多个 AI 编程助手近期完成的任务。 一条命令继续之前的工作：voyager continue 会自动寻找最近的会话。对于支持原生恢复的 Agent，会直接调用对应的 Resume 功能；对于无法直接恢复的 Agent，则自动生成 Handoff Context Package。 跨 Agent Handoff：可以把一次会话整理成包含任务目标、修改文件、执行命令、错误信息以及当前进度的 Context Package，再交给 Codex、Claude Code、Grok 等其他 Agent 接着完成。 原生恢复历史会话：Voyager 会识别不同 Agent 自己的恢复方式，例如 codex resume、claude --resume、dsh --resume、grok -r 等，而不是重新模拟一份会话。 完整导出与文件追踪：支持将会话导出为方便阅读的 Markdown，或者包含标准化事件与原始数据的 JSON；还可以查看某次会话操作过哪些文件，并对 Claude Code 会话重建修改前后的 Diff。 Local First：所有 Agent 原始数据均以只读方式访问，索引完全保存在本地，无账号、无云端服务、无遥测，并支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux。

projects.title: Show HN: Godot and Rust based multiplexer (terminal panes and more)
projects.author: 1nv1n
projects.summary: I wanted to share my side-project: gPTY. Started off as an idea to combine Godot and Rust in a project (two stacks I wanted to use more to learn more). The base inspiration was tmux - simply allow spawning multiple PTYs and then let the user grid/tile them how they see fit. But since we have the Godot game engine at our disposal, we can do some more interesting things, like add an FPS counter, and then subsequently also let people set their preferred FPS (the idea being the potential lower power draw if someone's running it on a laptop on battery power vs someone running it on a desktop with high/native FPS). In its current state, with me using Oh-my-Pi a lot, it's evolving into a terminal workspace that can be used for orchestrating autonomous AI agents by way of dogfooding (or you know, just run herdr inside of gPTY - it's the better orchestrator and just good software - I found it after starting this project, and now I'm finding myself using it a lot). Also, we're not limited to just terminals. Since we have Godot, we have basically a 2D (and potentially a 3D) canvas to play with. We can already full-screen the app for "zen" mode, no taskbar, no distractions. TUI die-hards can have their media or other apps entirely in terminal panes. There has been some ground-work on getting Markdowns displayed properly done and I want to work on some kind of Wiki framework for local knowledge-management next, then create more types of panes (think native audio/video on a media pane, that sits alongside your terminal pane), and some simple 2D games (like snake) to prototype. More details are on the ROADMAP. What's not easy (and probably won't happen) is a browser. Having done a couple of (small) projects using Electron already, the temptation to ditch Godot/Rust (learning curve) did come up (and also the ecosystem, the ease with which I could pull components and use web technologies - development velocity would definitely be higher there). But on the flipside, given all of the available LLM and AI support that we are privileged to have today, I figured the velocity should be comparable depending on how much I leaned on those. And lean I did. Godot/Rust seemed the better call to me and my intent anyway - going with the 'it's not just the end but the journey that matters' philosophy. So yes, there has been heavy use of LLMs & AI to generate a lot of the code. But I do review and steer actively, not relying solely on vibes, and there's a few bits here & there that have been human authored. There are definitely a lot of polish and QoL items that need to land to make the end user experience better, but in the meantime, let me know your thoughts and/or concerns! Repository: https://github.com/godot-pty/gpty Docs/Blog: https://godot-pty.github.io/gpty/

projects.title: Show HN: MySamantha – a productivity app where the AI is optional
projects.author: thejasonsamuel
projects.summary: Most of the recent tools being developed are versions of the personal assistant that everyone has been promising for a long time. I see ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Instinct (now viral), Muse, and many more. When I started to build MySamantha I thought about building a personal assistant as well. Connect email and calendar accounts to it, add some memory and context, give it some tools and it'll do things for you. I did launch it before here, and we realized that we were putting the least permanent part of the system at the center. I started wondering why the Assistant had to be the main product? But before that, why do I need a personal assistant? I was on team productivity before and I only wanted the AI to make me more productive. I had Notion, Obsidian, Todoist and I used them to be more productive at work and since ChatGPT came, I started using that heavily. But one thing that continued to piss me off is the fact that I am unable to share context between what I wanted to do. Sure, I am going to complain what each of these productivity apps did. Every productivity app had so much enshittification with AI stuffed down my throat that even though I love AI, I stopped going into those apps. Agents and shit. I don't need that, give me back my simple note taking app which I always loved. Their MCPs? No. I had context all over. I wanted something simple. With Models increasing intelligence day by day and labs releasing more and more models, there's one thing I knew for sure. Idk which model I'll be using two years from now. But I know I'll still have my emails, calendars, notes, documents, tasks, meetings and everything I've accumulated. So we started building MySamantha around that instead. Instead of a separate Notes app, Todo app, Email client or Calendar for everything, we built a place where I can work on all at the same place. Combine AI, connect my emails, my calendars associated with my work email, my Meeting Recorder are all here. At the same time, we don't want "everything in one place" to mean everything is stuck here. You can import from Notion, back your notes to both Notion and Google drive (as Google Docs), your to-do from Todoist or Microsoft To-do, import your vault from Obsidian, enjoy the same knowledge graph as Obsidian does, Export, etc., MySamantha sits on top of this. You can use any models. Bring your OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or even pay-as-you-go. If another model becomes better, change it. Don't like AI? switch it off. The product still works. The best part? everything is here in one place. Compare the meeting notes I had with the email I received to draft an email? yup, done. All context in one place. The Assistant becomes more useful, the more it knows about you. No model lock-ins. A pure productivity personal workspace where you can switch AI off if you don't need it. Feel free to check out what we're trying at https://mysamantha.ai Curious to know what HN thinks about this. Feedbacks and Queries welcome.

AST 只提供精准定位 ContextOS 给 Codex 的是 path::symbol、函数签名和行号范围，不是完整实现代码。编辑器打开的是具体目标方法，不是整个文件。 4. runcommand 压缩命令输出 命令执行结果会经过 ContextOS 的终端网关，过滤 ANSI、进度条、本地路径和重复日志，只保留结构化诊断信息。 5. 测试回执决定完成状态 完成状态绑定测试执行结果和检查点。源码改过以后，相关检查点会变成 retestrequired，模型不能只靠“我觉得完成了”过关。 对比 | 环节 | 不使用 ContextOS | 使用 ContextOS | 实测结果 | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 项目结构理解 | 每轮读目录和文件 | 读取 Git 追踪的项目图 | 不重复扫描 | | 代码定位 | 读取整个源码文件 | path::symbol + 行号 | 单任务上下文降低 99.4% | | 执行链上下文 | 返回多模块实现内容 | 只返回定位信息 | 执行链上下文降低 98.5% | | 命令输出 | 原始终端日志进入上下文 | runcommand 过滤和压缩 | 日志压缩 94.8% | | 完成状态 | 模型自我判断 | 测试回执 + 检查点门禁 | 目标模块召回 100% | 表格里的 99.4%、98.5%、94.8% 来自 npm run benchmark 的可复现实测；标题里的“综合减少 60%”是我长时间任务用下来的体感。 欢迎实际试一下，尤其是已经用 Codex 跑过中大型项目的人。

projects.title: Show HN: Charter – Operate production-safe agents that run on your own infra
projects.author: alama24
projects.summary: Even though everyone is talking about AI agents doing everything for them at work, many companies still aren't using autonomous agents to automate real operational work internally. Usually it's because of the complexity of bootstrapping an agent from scratch that’s production-safe (won’t spend all your company’s budget, burn through compute costs because it runs too often, or call a tool that breaks a customer). Even with today's agent-building frameworks, running agents reliably in production often means stitching together LangChain, Temporal, observability tools, approval systems, and custom guardrail logic. And that’s just for running an agent safely: there also has to be a management system so someone can observe and operate all their agents (upgrade it, roll it back, stop it). We wanted to build the end-to-end internal agent infrastructure that every company has to build today to use production-safe agents internally as an open-source platform. The important thing is that getting an agent running safely is quick and simple: someone can first define their agent tying it to a version, and their lifecycle and runtime policies in YAML. Next they register their agents on workers in YAML and run those workers wherever they want. This means that if one AKS cluster has permissions for the tools needed for agents X and Y and another has permissions for agents A and B, they would each register those agents on their respective clusters. Finally they can use the CLI to apply and run the agent, and then manage it with approvals, responding to questions its asking, upgrade it/roll it back/pause it (via either CLI or a UI/portal running on localhost that are communicating with the control plane). Some of the agent lifecycle management can be automated by the system: metric-based lifecycle policies make it so a user can say “if this new agent version I’m trying out (with a different prompt) fails 10 times, roll it back to the old version” or “if the new agent version is spending over a certain amount in the last 5 runs block it from being run anymore till I debug and resume it”. This is useful for teams that want to run many agents without needing someone on standby to intervene if something goes wrong on any one of them. The control plane is self-hostable or can be run via a managed cloud offering, and the self-hostable option combined with someone doing local inference is actually a completely air-gapped system. Give it a try: https://github.com/boundflow/charter and let us know what you think.

projects.title: Show HN: Nightshift – Rust CLI to Orchestrate GitHub Issue Resolution with Dags
projects.author: shaurya-sethi
projects.summary: Hi everyone, I built Nightshift: An agent-agnostic rust-cli tool that orchestrates completion of GitHub Issues. When Openai and Anthropic released `/goal` a couple months ago, I was really excited to try it for long-horizon tasks. But after using it, it didn't blow me away and i did some digging and found a major architectural flaw when using it for complex multi-issue workflows: context rot. This isn't anything new, but given how openai positioned this feature to developers, i was let down by how they'd implemented context management. Though `goal/` is a step forward in long-horizon coding, it lacks task decomposition and proper handling of context - it uses a multi-tier approach that includes persistent context chaining (PCC) to memory, local vector embeddings for RAG, sliding windows, and compaction. In principle, giving claude/codex a directive of `/goal work towards closing my open issues on github` should work but this specific execution model hits a fatal wall - Even with massive context windows and RAG, llm reasoning quality degrades significantly beyond 150k~ tokens, the agent continues working with worsening performance and finally to prevent token exhaustion it uses compaction to summarize old logs. In practice, this causes compaction amnesia. The model is asked to summarize a massive blob of mixed-relevance information when its reasoning quality is already at its lowest. This compaction leads to forgetting critical constraints, makes way for hallucinations of past decisions, and introduces noise that makes the new context unreliable for long-horizon work. I made nightshift to handle the "outer-loop" and enforce strict session boundaries. So rather than getting one agent to work towards closing issues in a single session, nightshift isolates the work like this: 1. You write a PRD as a parent Github issue that defines what needs to be implemented and break it down into vertically sliced child issues with explicit kanban-style dependencies. 2. You run `nightshift --prd 1 --agent claude` 3. nightshift utilises `gh` cli to resolve the dependency graph and pick the next unblocked issue. 4. it syncs the repo, puts together essential context for just that issue and starts a new agent session piping the prd and issue context directly to stdin for the agent to pick up. 5. the agent is now responsible for the usual coding - new feature branch, implementation and testing, pr and self-review, and finally closes the issue. 6. nightshift finds the next unblocked issue after maintaining git hygiene and loops until all issues linked to the prd are resolved. Its a very simple orchestration, but its effective. The agent has no memory of previous runs and it doesn't need to - each task is isolated and gets a fresh agent session. The state is managed entirely through filesystem and git operations and you get determinstic scheduling, failure isolation, and robust autonomy. It currently supports claude-code, codex, cursor, antigravity, pi, opencode, and github-copilot and im working on adding support for more agents as this project grows. With all that being said, I'd like to close with saying that this doesn't replace or compete with our favourite coding tools - just extends their capabilities. Its an opinionated tool and not as flexible as `/goal` which is still better for repetitive tasks wherein number of iterations are discovered by actually doing the work and you cannot meaningfully plan this. It isn’t a better goal - just makes goal-driven coding work more disciplined. I think if you've already taken the time to plan everything ahead, implementation can be handed off to an agent as long as there is proper context management which keeps the costs and quality in control. I'd love to hear your thoughts on this and check out your experiments with long-horizon task orchestration. Maybe the way going forward is combining macro management with micro management? Thanks.

projects.title: Show HN: MaruCheck – Independent QA for AI-generated code
projects.author: KidusMT
projects.summary: Hi HN, I've been building MaruCheck, an independent, open-source QA verification tool aimed to solve the issues that arise when coding agents like codex, claude, cursor make semantic issues that has heavy ramifications. Take the example where the requirements says a free user gets 5 uploads. The code changes this behavior to 10. Test generated from the implementation may simply start expecting 10. But Marucheck treats the existing approved requirements as a separate evidence and flags the behavior change. Some of the things implemented currently are Quality contracts, repository and stack scanning, Git diff/change- impact analysis, risk based analysis, semantic drift detection, QA memory for previous bugs/regression, CLI workflows, integration for coding agents, Github/CI verification etc etc.. Another area I’m experimenting with is QA Memory. If six months ago a bug existed because users could access another customer’s invoice by changing an invoice ID, MaruCheck can associate that regression with the relevant files/contracts. If those areas change again later, that previous failure becomes part of the new verification plan. The project is local-first and I’m trying not to reinvent existing testing infrastructure unnecessarily. The idea is to orchestrate tools like Playwright/Vitest/security/Jest tooling rather than build another browser automation framework from scratch. Currently it's on NPM and you can runit using npx or npm by writiing npx --yes marucheck@0.3.0 init and all the information and docs are available on the site marucheck.dev. projects.summary: 开了十几个 Claude Code 终端之后，我发现要管的不是终端，而是正在推进的工作：哪个会话在等我拍板、哪个跑挂了、这个方案是从哪个会话分出来的。于是写了码头（Matou），一个 macOS 上的 Claude Code 多会话桌面工作台，开源 GPL-3。 三个视图看同一批会话 会话卡片：每个 Claude Code 会话是一张卡片，横向滑动切换，同时和多个会话对话。卡片之间可以用自然语言互相读屏、互相派活，不用复制粘贴。 思维轨迹 DAG：从一个会话 fork 出子会话去试不同方案，fork 关系画成有向图，一眼看到方案 A 在跑、方案 B 卡住、回归失败，点节点直接落到那张卡片。 项目看板：事项拖进「进行中 / 阻塞 / 完成」，管的是项目周期，不是终端窗口。 其他 分级通知：只在需要你拍板时打断，其余静默计数。 Fork 子会话自动配 Git Worktree，多方案互不污染。 重启后页签、分屏、目录、输出原样恢复。 当前仅支持 macOS（Apple Silicon），Electron + React + TypeScript。 安装包见 Releases，欢迎试用和提 issue。

projects.title: Show HN: Maxxwell – The IDE for Optimal Tokenmaxxing
projects.author: mys1
projects.summary: Hi HN! I’m Michael, one of the founders of Rindler (YC S26). We built Maxxwell, which helps you manage a dozen coding-agent sessions’ progress, context, and blockers. This lets you spend more time with the actual high-leverage decisions (and gives you more confidence in stepping away from your computer). We were originally building browser agents that log in to sites with a cached representation of the site to make for cheap and reliable repeat runs. There were a ton of hard challenges like mapping sites, getting past bot defenses, and handling credentialing and 2FA. There was a huge maintenance surface, and we were getting bogged down with technical deliverables. We tried Cursor, Claude Code, Conductor, and even built an internal Devin. These tools either felt like they were too slow to iterate through large tasks, or became black boxes that I just couldn’t trust with their decisioning (you can’t just tell Devin to “improve the site mapper” and call it a day, unfortunately). So, we eventually settled on twelve Claude Code sessions running across our terminal panes. You get more control over the work being done while still multiplying your output volume, albeit at a cost: you. Answering questions across twelve terminals is really draining. Also, a lot of the questions are niche code choices that crowd out the stuff actually worth your opinion. It’s not immediately obvious which sessions are making progress, which are stuck on something trivial, or which are getting lost in the sauce of making up new goals. Lastly, I just felt less like a conductor of agents and more like just the human medium connecting Claude to my workspace. In the pursuit of touching grass again, we jerry-rigged our own system, which has an orchestrator agent focused on keeping other sessions aligned towards their goals and parsing through the agent noise. Now, I primarily message that one orchestrator session alone. It tells me what’s landed, what’s been decided for me, and what actually needs my input. Every worker is an unmodified Claude or Codex process in a real PTY, so you can still attach to any session and interface with it. This functionally results in all the productivity and quality benefits of multiplexing sessions while hopefully keeping you sane. Here's a 90 second walkthrough of the IDE: https://www.loom.com/share/125c58d597234685b1a632839a83813a In the last month that we’ve been using this, merged PRs per prompt (at similar semantic weight) has gone from 0.9 to 5, and our revert rate of said PRs has fallen from 0.56% to 0.20%. We are confident letting the orchestrator manage our agent sessions for hours at a time, and it works quite well for overnight runs too. Maxxwell is BYOK or subscription, and otherwise free and fully local. We’re considering making a hosted service as well to save your local machine’s memory. Check it out! If you’re already running several agent sessions at once, I’d especially like to know: - What would make you trust that an unattended session stayed aligned? We currently have per-goal checklists that the orchestrator monitors to ensure adherence. - What’s your preferred balance of agent autonomy and control?

projects.title: Show HN: MaskShift – a maximalist coding agent with zero NPM dependencies
projects.author: Nafeeur
projects.summary: MaskShift is a local-first coding agent harness. Features: - Works with models that have no tool-calling API. Tool schemas are rendered into the system prompt and the model calls them by writing a block in its reply, parsed back into a normal tool call. - No npm runtime dependencies. Daemon are Node 22 built-ins only. Install is a file copy and a symlink. - Multi-provider: Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, LM Studio, vLLM. - 148 native tools: filesystem, shell, search/indexing, Git and Workspace, LSP, browser/CDP, containers, SSH, databases, web fetch. - Lazy MCP loading. Catalog is searched, the relevant server connects on demand, only those tools enter the context window. - 36 bundled skills, plus skills imported from Claude, Codex, and Copilot directories. - Bridges to Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, and Aider when they're on PATH. - Scheduled automations, plugins, persistent memory, parallel agents in isolated worktrees. - Web cockpit with live run telemetry, plan pane, tool traces, source browser, and a host terminal. Permissive by default. No per-command approval. Recovery is pre-run checkpoints, Git stash refs, and an append-only audit log. Keep it on loopback or in the container.

projects.title: Show HN: Ontoplano, FOSS Life Management desktop and mobile app with MCP server
projects.author: chedieck
projects.summary: Hi, I am Estevão, the developer of Ontoplano, a holistic life management webapp, supporting *tasks planning, todos, goals, habits, notebooks, people, inventory tracking, recipes, and more.* I built this app because my life was spread over multiple different apps and pieces of paper. Ontoplano started as a weekly planner that I made (because I dislike sharing my life information with Google and also had nitpicks with every FOSS calendar I tried) and grew into one app for everything personal. As said in the title, the project is completely free and open source, licensed under AGPL-3.0, for anyone who wants to run their own instance. I run my own instance at app.ontoplano.com, for people who aren't into self hosting. On it, there are no ads, no tracking/profiling code, no telemetry, no tricks whatsoever. You can leave it at any time and take all your data with you. I firmly believe software should empower people, not exploit them, and I hope that's just what I can provide the world with by releasing Ontoplano. Furthermore, I also like software to be beautiful and practical. Ontoplano (self-hosted or not) comes with a Mobile app (PWA or the APK if you want the widget and prettier-looking notifications), and a MCP server for using it with AI (if you hate AI, don't worry, there is no built-in AI to opt-out of, only a MCP server you can create a token for, or not). I implemented these two because: 1. I wanted to use it smoothly, even if I am away from home 2. Sometimes is much easier to say "Hey AI, put on Ontoplano that last week I actually slacked off and played videogames everyday" than manually doing that in a calendar, for psychological and time-consuming reasons. Besides that, you can also: - Import your notes/todo tasks from Google Tasks, Google Keep, Obsidian, Todoist, and more in the future. - Calendar sync with Google Calendar (or other calendars) using ICS - Access your shopping list offline it, and share it with your family members (if you want to). And there is more in the roadmap. Any help is appreciated — be it you self-hosting to help me find bugs and improve the app, be it you giving me a star on GitHub. Thank you for your attention. Main website: https://ontoplano.com Demo (no signup, throwaway account): https://demo.ontoplano.com Code: https://github.com/ontoplano/ontoplano Docs: https://docs.ontoplano.com

projects.title: 【开源自荐】PolyJump：可配置 三维 棋盘游戏 AI 研究环境
projects.author: SanZiNEO

github.name: SanZiNEO/poly-jump
github.description: A configurable 3D jump-chess framework with A/B geometries, multi-player rule switches, and RL/self-play training support.

projects.summary: 我是 PolyJump 的开发者，自荐一个开源项目：PolyJump。 它不是又一个 2D 跳棋游戏，而是一个“不同空间路径模型 + 可配置规则 + 多人博弈”的 3D 棋盘 AI 研究环境。 传统棋类大多建立在二维平面上；即使一些项目标着“3D”，也大多只是把多个二维面组装成一个三维外形，展开后仍然是一张平面。PolyJump 不只是在视觉上做 3D，而是把棋盘本身的空间路径结构作为可配置变量——不同的空间路径模型、2/3/4/6/8 人局、多种移动方向、中国跳棋 / 西洋跳棋 / 混合规则，让 AI 面对的不再是固定环境，而是多智能体、需要空间规划和搜索的博弈任务。 在线试玩 👉 效果 功能 7 种空间路径模型：A / B / C / D + A-ext / B-ext / C-ext 移动方向：6 / 8 / 12 / 14 / 18 / 20 / 26，根据模型自动匹配或自定义 玩家数：2 / 3 / 4 / 6 / 8 移动规则：普通移动、跳跃、连跳、两格跳、自由停、强制跳到底 游戏模式：中国跳棋、西洋跳棋（吃子）、混合模式 积分制：连跳、吃子、进目标区、胜利奖励，可配置开关 3D 前端：HTML + Three.js，渲染、合法路径高亮、AI 自动对弈、回放、中英文切换 后端：Python + FastAPI，HTTP API 和纯后端 GameEnv AI 研究：airesearch/ 基准评测，支持批量对局、指标统计、时间戳归档 一个初步发现 同一个 MCTS 搜索算法放在 A / B / C / D 四种几何模型上，路径选择会系统性不同： A / D：MCTS 更容易找到更短路径 B / C：MCTS 更容易走长连跳，detour 更高 这说明几何结构本身就会影响 AI 的空间规划策略。 完整报告：docs/11-cross-geometry-discovery.md AI / 研究接口 外部程序可以通过 Python 接口直接驱动游戏： python from backend.game.config import PolyJumpConfig from backend.game.env import GameEnv config = PolyJumpConfig(geometry="B", bradius=6, players=2) env = GameEnv(config) obs = env.reset() while not obs.done: actions = obs.legalactions 接入你的 AI：MCTS / RL / LLM Agent 等 action = actions[0] obs = env.executeaction(action) airesearch/ 提供不依赖前端的批量评测，目前包含： random / manhattan / euclidean / chebyshev / graphbfs MCTS 搜索 baseline PettingZoo AEC 包装（fullaction / primitive） 输出胜率、action/step 指标、路径距离、目标区进出指标，结果归档到 airesearch/runs/<时间戳>/。 快速开始 bash pip install -r requirements.txt python run.py

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Super：用 Rust 写的 API-First 进程编排器 —— Supervisor / PM2 的现代替代品
projects.author: hzbd

github.name: schiplat/super
github.description: The API-First, Lightweight Process Orchestrator for the Edge.

projects.summary: 背景介绍 每台服务器上，总有一批需要“长期活着”的进程：自建网关、队列 Worker、边缘采集脚本、或者本地运行的模型推理服务。 管好这些进程，大家通常会选择经典的 Supervisor 或 PM2： 但 PM2 拖家带口带着庞大的 Node.js 运行时，在精简 VPS 或边缘设备上显得格外沉重； Supervisor 的配置和体验还停留在 ini / CLI 时代，缺乏原生的现代 HTTP API，CI/CD 和 Agent 很难通过代码灵活操控； 至于 systemd，它虽强大但强依赖 root 权限，不跨平台，且动态管理进程门槛高；而 Docker Compose 有时又显得杀鸡用牛刀，很多人并不想为了两个常驻脚本去承受构建镜像的额外开销。 为了兼顾“极致轻量”与“可编程性”，我们用 Rust 编写了 Super：一个无额外运行时依赖的 API-First 轻量进程编排器。 架构设计：极简清晰的双二进制 Super 采用了经典的 Daemon-Client（守护进程 + 客户端） 架构，打包发布为两个独立的纯静态二进制文件： superd（后台引擎 / Daemon）： 核心守护进程，通常作为开机自启系统服务静默运行。它负责进程生命周期托管、健康检测、崩溃重启、日志汇聚与安全沙箱，并对外暴露统一规范的 REST API & WebSocket。 super（命令行客户端 / CLI）： 提供给开发者操作的终端工具。super 本身不直接拉起进程，它只是 superd 的一个官方 HTTP API 客户端。 这意味着：你在 CLI 里能做的一切，CI 流水线、自动运维脚本、或者外部 Agent 都可以无缝直接调用 superd 的 API 实现。 核心特性 Rust 纯静态编译，零运行时依赖：无 Python、Node 等环境依赖，只有 superd 和 super 两个体积精巧的二进制文件，极简容器、精简 VPS、边缘盒子直接开箱即用。 API-First（进程即可编程资源）： 单行命令托管：super add --name demo --autostart python3 -m http.server 8080； 声明式栈管理：支持通过 TOML 声明服务依赖链、健康检查与环境变量，一条 super apply 一键收敛整套服务栈； 原生标准接口：彻底告别解析 CLI 终端文本输出的时代，所有状态查询与管理均走标准 HTTP/WS。 崩溃自愈与稳健守护：异常退出自动拉起、退出码判断、启动时延防护、优雅停机（SIGTERM ➔ 超时 SIGKILL），该有的守护逻辑一个不少。 平滑无损发布（事务式更新）：服务版本更新内置事务保障：“备份 ➔ 校验 ➔ 切换 ➔ 失败自动回滚”，告别手工替换文件重启赌命的裸奔操作。 可观测性与事件账本（Audit Ledger）：实时日志流（WebSocket）、历史日志检索；内置事件账本，记录服务状态变更的完整因果链，出事能复盘，不靠盲猜。 默认安全：superd 默认仅监听本地 Loopback 地址（可按需配置监听外网并启用鉴权）；敏感环境变量在 API 与 CLI 输出中自动脱敏打码。 一条命令自动注册系统服务：安装脚本在校验 SHA-256 后，会自动将 superd 注册为各平台的系统自启服务（Linux systemd / macOS launchd / FreeBSD rc.d），开机自启无需手写 unit。 快速上手 1. 一键脚本安装（推荐） 通过官方自动化脚本完成安装（自动校验 SHA-256 并注册 superd 为系统开机自启服务，非 root 用户可能需要 sudo 权限）： bash curl -fsSL | sh 2. 手动下载与安装 若处于离线环境或需要手动分发部署： 下载预编译包：前往 GitHub Releases 页面 下载对应系统架构的二进制包（提供 Linux x8664/arm64、macOS、FreeBSD 的 .tar.gz 及 SHA-256 校验和文件）； 完整安装与配置指南：手动解压后的二进制文件放置位置、权限设置及自启服务注册步骤，请参考官方文档：快速开始与安装指南（Getting Started）。 3. 基础管理操作 托管并拉起一个常驻服务： bash 通过 super CLI 向 superd 注册并自动拉起服务 super add --name demo --autostart python3 -m http.server 8080 查看当前运行与健康状态 super list 实时追踪日志流 super logs demo --tail AI 协作彩蛋：项目根目录维护了一份针对 AI 上下文工程优化的 SKILL.md。你可以直接把它喂给 Cursor、Claude 或 ChatGPT，让你的 AI 助手瞬间掌握 Super 的所有规范，秒级帮你编写编排配置与排障指令。 当前状态与平台支持 系统支持：支持 Linux (x8664 / arm64)、macOS、FreeBSD；Windows 推荐使用官方 Docker 镜像运行。 阶段说明：项目目前处于公测阶段，核心编排与 API 路径有较完整的集成测试覆盖，且在作者团队的自有服务中日常运行。但仍建议大家优先在开发环境、Staging 或非核心负载上试用。 现阶段大家的每一次试用、批评和提 Issue，都是对项目最大的帮助与支持！ GitHub schiplat/super 版本发布（Releases）：github.com/schiplat/super/releases 快速安装指南：super.docs.sconts.com/docs/01-getting-started/ 完整文档站：super.docs.sconts.com

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Minta：Agent 的"记忆管理员"，不只是存记忆
projects.author: xinchen03

github.name: xinchen03/minta
github.description: The context quality layer for AI agents — memory that checks itself: lifecycle governance, calibrated confidence, and   staged claim gates. Local-first, MCP 19 tools, DeepSeek Harness plugin.

projects.summary: 我是 Minta 的开发者，自荐一个开源项目：Minta ()——面向 AI 智能体的上下文质量层。 一句话：它不只是又一款 AI 记忆库，而是给记忆做生命周期管理的质量层——检测"哪条记忆已经过期、哪两条在互相打架、哪件事 AI 根本没做过却声称做过"。 记忆工具教不会 AI 记忆,几乎所有的记忆工具都在解决"怎么记住"。这是我跟"记不住"这件事死磕三个月，逼出来的结论。你叫它"别动 tests 目录"：它学了。可它不知道的是，可能这条规则已经过时了，因为你上个月早就改主意了；又或者，它把三个月前试错的旧方案，当成宝贝推荐给你。而且上午刚讲过的话，下午新会话又问你一遍。 所以，存得住 ≠ 信得过。Minta的做法： 过期检测：定期扫描，把过时的记忆标记、归档——不靠 LLM 自己"觉得"过时了 冲突表面化：两条记忆矛盾时，不把两个都塞回 prompt，而是摊开给你决定 纠正闭环：你纠正 AI → 进收件箱 → 你确认 → 变成规则。一次纠正，长期生效 证据分级：按证据强度设门控，"没做过实验的事，不允许声称做过" 60 秒本地跑起来，无云、免费： bash git clone && cd minta python mintacli.py start # MCP 工具，Claude Code / Codex / Cursor 直接接 3 分钟接入（Windows 实测一键）： github.com/xinchen03/minta → Download ZIP → 解压 双击 startminta.bat（自动装依赖，弹网页+菜单） 菜单选编辑器：Claude Code / Codex / DeepSeek Harness / Cursor 了解更多：awesome-dsh-plugin.com/p/xinchen03/minta--dsh-plugin/ DSH 用户安装：dsh plugin --profile web add @xxinchen/dsh-plugin Context Health——记忆生命周期仪表盘 () 核心引擎和记忆中枢 UI 全部开源；研究驾驶舱等高级面板通过 API Key 激活。项目还很新——但"记忆会过期、会打架、会自说自话"这个问题，大概每个把重要事情交给 AI 的人都会撞上，也许值得一看。

projects.author: jo32

projects.summary: 同时开五六个 Claude Code / Codex 在不同 git worktree 里干活的时候，最大的问题不是工具不好用，而是不知道该看哪个窗口。终端长得都一样，只能一个个切过去看最后一行输出。tmux 能管窗口，但它不知道「agent 在等你确认」这件事，对 tmux 来说卡在权限询问的 Claude 和正在写代码的 Claude 没有区别。 Seahelm 把这件事变成一眼可见：每个 repo 一个 tab，每个 git worktree 一张卡片，卡片上只显示 running / waiting / broken 三种状态。 技术上有两点可能值得一提。 一是终端渲染直接嵌了 libghostty（Ghostty 的 C 接口），Swift + AppKit，不是 Electron，延迟和渲染是原生终端的水平。会话持久化用 zmx，退出 App 或者重启电脑之后 agent 还在原地。 二是状态判断做成了一个优先级梯子：进程退出状态 > OSC 133 shell 集成标记 > 文本正则匹配。正则那一层是数据驱动的，每个 agent 一份 JSON manifest，可以在 ~/.config/seahelm/agents/ 下覆盖。Claude Code 和 Codex 接了原生 hook，所以「在等你」是一个真实事件，不是从屏幕文字猜出来的。目前 12 个 agent 有状态识别：claude、codex、opencode、gemini、cursor、aider、amp、cline、goose、kiro、pi、agent。 另外 agent 可以反过来操作它。每个 pane 都有 SEAHELMPANEID，配一个控制 socket 和 CLI： seahelm pane split <pane> --direction right seahelm pane run <pane> "npm test" seahelm wait agent-status <pane> --status Idle 所以一个 agent 能自己开一个兄弟 pane、把活派过去、然后等它做完。

projects.title: Show HN: Votito helps you decide what to build next with confidence
projects.author: gojkoa
projects.summary: Hey HN, We're finally launching Votito, after about a year of development, as it's now (almost) polished enough for other people to use. I'd love your feedback! AI tools make software faster to write, so the constraint is no longer building things. It is knowing which things deserve to be built. Votito aims to be a "product decision platform" to help figure that out. Having previously built two relatively successful SaaS products, we've spent a ton of time figuring out what users need, collecting feedback and trying to turn signals from the user community into actionable ideas, using a bunch of disconnected tools and half-baked scripts. We've consolidated those internal tools and processes into an online idea management system, combining user feedback with product research, so product teams can engage their users easily. Votito is not trying to compete with task management tools like Jira and Linear, but to work in the area before the backlog, in the "weak commitment" zone where unstructured proposals need to mature to become implementable ideas. Throw random stakeholder demands, user suggestions and feature requests into Votito and let them marinate until they become something useful, if they ever do. Votito will help you spot the gems that deserve your attention. It will also stop garbage from going into your actual task tracking tools, and prevent people from being overwhelmed with managing bad ideas. While the product is naturally oriented towards PMs, we're betting on the trend that teams are becoming smaller with AI support, and that people inside delivery teams will need to take on most traditional product responsibilities in the future. The Wall Street Journal recently reported on the trend of "pods" of 3-4 people augmented with AI agents taking on the tasks that previously needed much larger groups. When teams have 10-15 people, companies can justify assigning a dedicated product person. But with 3-4 people per pod, this is just not feasible. GitHub's research from December 2025 found that developers will increasingly need to think at the level of "understanding user needs". One of our goals is to put proven product methods and tools into the hands of people who are not traditional product managers, making it easy to discover and apply the right tools and, crucially, to understand the results. Here are 5 ways Votito can help you decide what to build next: - Collect evidence with ideas to help you prove that things are worth building. Evidence can be as simple as a list of interested customers, external documents such as market research, or something as complex as the result of an A/B test. - Score ideas automatically based on impact, effort and evidence. We provide two popular confidence models out of the box to help you get started. - Engage users or stakeholders to vote on ideas for additional confidence signals. - Keep the community engaged. Let people propose new ideas directly in Votito, comment and vote on other people's proposals. Publishing a roadmap of ideas you've accepted into development, and a changelog of features you delivered recently. - Conduct deep research with proven product management surveys. Feature requests are pointers that something is interesting, but they are rarely complete information, or even the best solutions for the problem. Votito allows you to easily run online surveys with people who voted on a proposal. We provide a collection of ready-made templates for major product management research tasks. You could, of course, set up a similar survey on another platform, but the difference is that we'll help you interpret the data, showing the best ways to score domain-specific surveys and evaluate statistical significance. The free version includes pretty much everything you need to run all the things mentioned above, with data retention of up to six months.

projects.title: Show HN: A Context Registry for AI coding agents
projects.author: sohaibtariq
projects.summary: Hi HN. We built an API context registry to help coding agents (like Claude Code) generate production-ready API integration code without blowing through token limits. We build a lot of API integrations. In our experience, most coding agents write basic client calls fine, but consistently stumble on details that make code shippable, like idempotent retries, rate-limiting and Auth token management. We tried all the existing approaches of injecting context into coding sessions: - Markdown dumps delivered via MCP (think Context7 or Mintlify Docs MCP) - API behaviour described in prose using AGENTS.md and skills. - OpenAPI specs However, all of them left the same production-readiness gaps. So we came up with our own approach that combines prose with typed SDK reference code into a "Context Plugin". You install the plugin into your coding agent and it automatically injects language-specific context whenever the agent works on an API. Across our benchmarks, Context Plugins boosted one-shot production readiness by up to 34%, allowing Sonnet to match or beat baseline Opus on the same integration tasks. You can read more about our experiments here https://www.apimatic.io/blog/working-api-call-is-not-product... We have published Context Plugins for 24 APIs for the community to try out, including Slack, Google Maps, and Notion. We'd love for you to give them a go and share your feedback on our plugins as well as our evaluation methodology.
